what_this_is: A DESIGN-FOR-ECO REQUIREMENT, declared for a tape-out-bound design. It is the input the `eco_readiness` feasibility axis compares a candidate against. It is not a default, not a fallback, and no program contains any of these numbers: a design that does not declare a requirement gets NOT_APPLICABLE from that axis, not this document.
authored_for: the re-adjudication of the five published cross-layer arms under ppa-crosslayer/eco-readjudication/. The design's own input documents (input/docs/L1..L9) declare NO design-for-ECO requirement, which is itself the finding: nothing the search could read said the spare population was required, so nothing stopped an arm deleting it.
not_derived_from_the_baseline: These numbers are argued from the methodology cited below, not read off the shipped default run. That the shipped default happens to carry exactly this population is a coincidence worth reporting and not the derivation -- a requirement inferred from a baseline is a requirement that says only `do what you already did`, and it can never be wrong.

eco_readiness.declared_by: the re-adjudication author, for a design whose own L2 names a primary tape-out target

why_each_number.min_spare_cells: The design places ~460-490 standard cells. The methodology band is ~1-5% of placed cells, starting at ~2-3%; 10 spares is ~2% of ~490 and sits at the bottom of that band. A floor at the bottom of the band is the weakest requirement that is still a requirement, which is the right place for a floor whose job is to refuse deletion rather than to dictate a budget.
why_each_number.min_spare_cells_by_kind: A repair needs a gate of the right FUNCTION. The methodology's mix is many inverters plus NAND2/NOR2 as the workhorses, with a useful few of mux2 / AOI / OAI and at least one flop, because a bug that needs a register cannot be fixed with combinational spares however many there are. Ten spares that are all inverters clear a count floor and cannot repair a sequential defect, which is why the count alone is not the requirement.
why_each_number.min_distinct_positions: Spares clustered in one corner are reachable only from nets that happen to be near that corner. Three distinct positions across a three-row core is a weak spread requirement and still refuses the degenerate all-in-one-place case. It is a SPREAD requirement and explicitly not a reachability one -- see `not_required_because_not_measurable` below.
why_each_number.require_tie_off: An untied spare input is not a usable spare: it is a floating gate, a leakage path and an ERC/LVS failure. The methodology calls tie-off mandatory, and a population that is not tied off is not a population.

not_required_because_not_measurable.eco_reachability: Whether a metal-only ECO could route from a given failing net to a given spare depends on routing resources left around both, and nothing this flow emits is a routability answer. Requiring it here would be requiring something no run could ever prove, which turns an axis into a permanent refusal rather than a check.
not_required_because_not_measurable.kind_sufficiency: Whether this mix can implement the repairs this design will actually need is a judgement about future bugs. The declaration states a mix; it does not claim the mix is right.
not_required_because_not_measurable.min_spare_pads: This design is a core macro with no pad ring in the flow that produced these runs, so a reserved-pad count would be a requirement against an artefact the flow does not produce. The `spare_pads` metric is still emitted and reads 0 on every arm; it is reported and not required.

methodology_cited.kind_mix: inverter / nand2 / nor2 / dff / mux2 / aoi / oai
methodology_cited.tie_off: mandatory; an untied spare is not a usable spare
methodology_cited.distribution: spatially distributed across the placeable area, not one corner
